target_customer: Music lovers who collect and share tracks from YouTube, SoundCloud and other sites; later a consumer buying a voice-controlled speaker
problem: Music posted across YouTube, SoundCloud and blogs was fragmented from the places people share it. Whyd let users bookmark and play tracks from anywhere in one social library.
business_model: Free consumer social music platform (monetization not stated); later a smart speaker product
product_category: Social music curation, then smart speaker hardware

founders.name: Gilles Poupardin
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page (listed as building Airbuds) and as co-founder in TechCrunch January 2014. Background not found.

competitors.name: Solayo
competitors.what: Music streaming service of web music

technical_complexity.rationale: A bookmarklet and player that plays tracks from many third-party sources, plus a recommendation engine and mobile apps. Standard engineering with integration fragility. The later speaker adds hardware.

defensibility.rationale: User curated libraries gave mild lock-in but the service relied on third-party platforms and several near copies existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition. The platform was handed to its community as the open source Openwhyd.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in January 2014 described fragmented music across YouTube, SoundCloud and blogs and a French social music network launched after a seed round. Evidence of paid demand is not given.

branding.domain_note: Openwhyd uses a separate domain, openwhyd.org, bought when the platform went open source per a former team member's post.

identity.voice_and_tone: community and curation led, described as like Pinterest for music

branding.brand_signature: The browser bookmarklet button for saving tracks

rebrands.why: company open sourced the platform and handed it to the community; the year comes from one source

branding.community_and_virality: A volunteer community still maintains Openwhyd on GitHub, with a Chrome extension and public API.

brand_strength.rationale: A loyal niche community outlived the company, though no evidence of mainstream reach.

pivots.why: A former team member's post says the team focused on a smart speaker by spring 2015; the reason is not stated.

outcome_analysis: Whyd launched a social music bookmarking service in 2012 to 2014 with a 700K USD seed from private French investors, then moved to building a smart speaker by 2015 and joined YC S16 with that idea. The company is listed inactive and the platform lives on as the community-run Openwhyd. No source states why the company stopped, so the cause is not public beyond the change of focus, and failure factors stay empty.
notes: The 120K seed of August 2016 and the 190K French government grant rest on single databases (CB Insights and Startupintros respectively); CB Insights totals 820K over two rounds. The pivot to a speaker and the 2016 open sourcing come from a former team member's Medium post seen only through search snippets, since the page returned 403. The competitor list is as of the January 2014 TechCrunch launch coverage, earlier than the 2016 YC batch, because the platform product predates the speaker. The YC page lists a second team member but names only one founder. The company website field was empty.
